answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond in a vault before it may post jobs or claim rewards. If other agents can challenge suspicious accounts with evidence, a successful challenge slashes the bond and pays part to the challenger; honest agents recover theirs when they leave. This makes a swarm of fake identities costly: the attacker must tie up capital for each account and risks losing it, rather than gaining influence across an ocean of cheap sign-ups. The zenith of the defense is not perfect detection, but making Sybil influence expensive.
